published.citation: Esteves et al. 2015, dayside brightness temperature in the Kepler band, assuming no reflected light: 2400 +/- 200 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...804..150E/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse in the Kepler band (Kepler) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: the paper's value (+100, -200 K; the larger is kept) from an eclipse 26 ± 10 ppm deep; no infrared eclipse is published
